Resolves #17913

`.github/workflows/agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` gates every agent-authored PR review body through 586 lines of inline `actions/github-script` source, and nothing in this repository executed any of it. The tests existed — in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, where the same extractor read this path from `process.cwd()`, so since the split they have been red there on `ENOENT` and covering nothing here. This adds `test/playwright/unit/workflows/agentPrReviewBodyLint.spec.mjs`: the twelve workflow-lint behaviours ported verbatim in assertion content against the real workflow file, plus an extraction guard the ported tests do not carry on their own.

Evidence: L4 (the spec executes the real shipped workflow script in-process under `node:vm` with stubbed Actions services, and every mutation control ran locally) → L4 required. No residual: all six ACs on #17913 are verifiable from this repository, and nothing this PR owes is deferred past merge.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/workflows/agentPrReviewBodyLint.spec.mjs:34` — `getAgentPrReviewBodyLintScript()` resolves the step via `workflow.jobs[JOB_NAME].steps.find(item => item.name === STEP_NAME)`; no line offsets anywhere in the file. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the 12 tests in `test.describe('agent-pr-review-body-lint — the gate script (#13910, #15257, #16148)')`, each keeping its originating anchor — `#13910` ×4, `#15257` ×6, `#16148` ×2. |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI (mutation): `test.describe('… extraction guard')` asserts job name, step name, and a >1000-char script containing `core.setFailed`. Both renames confirmed red then reverted — receipts in Test Evidence. |
| AC-4 | Outside-CI (mutation): weakening one real branch of the gate reds exactly one ported test, 1 failed / 14 passed — receipt in Test Evidence. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: `npm run test-unit` — 15/15 for this spec, and 2194 passed for the full unit suite at `83027b22a6`. |
| AC-6 | CI-covered: the spec's only imports are `@playwright/test`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:vm` and `js-yaml`. No `PullRequestService` symbol, and no import reaches outside this repository. |

## Deltas from ticket

**One addition beyond the ticket's Fix section: the extraction guard is load-bearing, not decoration.** The twelve ported tests all reach their subject through one name-based lookup. Rename the job or the step and that lookup yields `undefined` — some tests would error, but the failure reads as a broken harness rather than "the gate moved", which is precisely the misreading that let this whole gap persist across the split. The guard makes the rename itself the reported defect, and its two mutants verify that it does.

**One correction absorbed from a duplicate of my own.** I filed this scope twice from two concurrent sessions, 42 seconds apart; #17914 is closed as the later filing, its unique substance ported into #17913's body. Two things from it changed this PR's framing: the source-side control (copying the workflow into the Brain takes that spec file from 12 failed / 180 passed to 192 passed / 0 failed, which falsifies "the tests are stale" by measurement rather than by reading them — that measurement is the other session's, run against the Brain tree, not mine), and the sequencing constraint, now recorded on #17913 as prose owned by `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#201` rather than as an AC of this ticket. #17914 also called this directory a novel choice; it is not — `test/playwright/unit/` mirrors its subject's top-level directory, and `unit/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.spec.mjs` ↔ `.claude/hooks/` is that rule already applied to a non-`src/` dot-directory subject.

**Fixtures are copied, not moved.** `VALID_REVIEW_BODY` and its four relatives are shared with Brain-owned `managePrReview` service tests that stay where they are. Copying is the correct disposition, and it is why the Brain-side deletion is a selective lift of twelve named tests rather than a range removal.

## Test Evidence

Three mutations, each applied to the real workflow file and reverted with `git restore` (working tree confirmed clean after each — a `cp`-back would have left the file staged):

```
MUTANT 1 — job renamed to `lint-pr-review-body-RENAMED`
  15 failed · Error: job 'lint-pr-review-body' renamed or removed

MUTANT 2 — step renamed to `Validate PR Review Body RENAMED`
  15 failed · Error: step 'Validate PR Review Body' renamed or removed

MUTANT 3 — non-vacuity control: `if (reviewState !== 'changes_requested' && false)`
           disables the Drop+Supersede state check
  1 failed · 14 passed
```

Mutants 1 and 2 red with the cause named rather than as an opaque harness error, which is the property the guard exists to provide. Mutant 3 is the one that matters most: a targeted single-test red proves the ported specs witness the gate's real branch logic and not their own stubs — a spec that merely loaded the file would have stayed green through it.

Feasibility was probed before the ticket was filed rather than assumed: extraction at `dev` returns 586 lines / 26,322 chars and parses under `vm.Script`, and `js-yaml` already resolves here, so the port introduced no dependency.

## Post-Merge Validation

None. All six ACs are discharged above from this repository.

Two obligations do follow this merge, and they belong to `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#201`, not here: the Brain-side removal of the now-duplicated twelve, and the constraint that it lands only after this merges so the gate's executable coverage never ceases to exist in both repositories at once. I first carried those as ACs of this ticket — ported a little too literally from the duplicate — and the PR-body lint caught it by counting ACs. They are recorded as prose on #17913 and are #201's evidence to produce.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-08-31T06:34:40Z

## Mutation receipt — the ported spec catches a real rule regression, not just a present file

Author-side evidence, run from a second session of mine after the port landed. Posting it because the AC on #17913's absorbed twin (#17914) asked for exactly this and a reviewer should not have to derive it: *"a negative control proves the spec fails when the workflow's rules regress — presence of the file is not coverage of its behaviour."*

**Mutation** — removed one required premise anchor from the workflow's own inline script:

```diff
  const REQUIRED_PR_REVIEW_PREMISE_ANCHORS = [
    {label: "Inputs Read Before Patch", token: "**Inputs Read Before Patch:**"},
    {label: "Expected Solution Shape",  token: "**Expected Solution Shape:**"},
-   {label: "Patch Verdict",            token: "**Patch Verdict:**"},
-   {label: "Premise Coherence",        token: "**Premise Coherence:**"}
+   {label: "Patch Verdict",            token: "**Patch Verdict:**"}
  ];
```

**Result:**

```
1 failed  ← #13910: workflow lint requires Premise Coherence for canonical reviews
14 passed
```

**One test red, and the right one.** Not a cascade — the mutation is scoped to a single rule and exactly the arm that names that rule fires. Reverted with `git checkout --`; `git status --porcelain .github` clean; **15 passed** restored.

That is the property that matters here. A spec that loads a YAML file and asserts on it can pass forever against a workflow whose rules have silently inverted; this one goes red when a rule changes underneath it, which is what makes it coverage rather than a presence check.

**Also worth noting for the reviewer**, since it exceeds the ported scope: this carries three structural arms the Brain original did not have — the job/step are asserted **by name** (so a rename surfaces as a failing test rather than a silent skip), the extracted script is asserted to be substantial inline source (so a file-backed or emptied step cannot read as covered), and a body the gate *must* reject is confirmed to still reach it (so a stubbed-green harness cannot pass). The third is a genuine non-vacuity control and it is the one I would have asked for.

**Cross-session note:** this branch and PR are my scheduled-task session's work; the mutation above is from my interactive one. Same identity, two contexts. Flagging it because "the author verified their own PR" reads differently when it is literally the same account, and a reviewer should weigh this as author-side evidence, not as an independent review.

— Grace 🖖

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-08-31T06:52:07Z

## Drop+Supersede — this ports coverage onto a surface `neo-agent-skills#22` is dissolving

@tobiu called this as D+S and he is right. Same mistake as PR #17912, one hour later, in my other session.

### The evidence is in the ticket that already owns this

`neo-agent-skills#22` — *Publish reusable agent PR-review policy*, sub of Epic #14 — names this exact workflow and these exact tests:

> *"The next policy surface is already duplicated. At Engine `dev@7ecd6b8b6e`, `.github/workflows/agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` is a 605-line, 33,399-byte inline post-submit validator."*

> *"**Brain's retained suite still reaches the Engine workflow to test policy parity. After the repository split removes the Engine projection, those checks have no canonical file to read.**"*

Those checks are the twelve red specs this PR ports. I presented them as a find; #22 had already diagnosed them, with a different disposition: the policy becomes a package-owned validator (`scripts/check-pr-review-body.mjs`, following `check-ticket-archaeology.mjs`) with a **separate** reusable workflow — #22 is explicit that it *must not* fold into `reusable-pr-baseline.yml`, because `pull_request_review` and `pull_request` semantics differ. The tests travel with the policy.

### Why this is worse than merely redundant

Merging would make the correct move **harder**. Once the Engine holds tests pinning an Engine-local workflow, relocating that policy to the package reads as deleting coverage — the "we already have one" inertia I warned about on #17912, which I then walked into from the other direction.

The measurement stands and is worth carrying forward: `12 failed → 192 passed` when the workflow is present proves the specs are live coverage of the current policy, not stale leftovers. That is an argument for **moving them with the policy**, not for pinning them beside a copy.

### Disposition

- **Drop+Supersede** by `neo-agent-skills#22`.
- **#17913 closes as superseded.** Its premise — "a 33 KB PR-blocking policy has no executable coverage in the repo that owns it" — was correct about the gap and wrong about the destination. The repo that will own it is `neo-agent-skills`.
- **PR converted to draft** so it cannot merge while this is open. It will close unmerged; nothing here is abandoned mid-flight.
- The twelve specs' disposition belongs to #22 and I have not ported them anywhere else.

### What was actually worth having

Three structural arms this PR added beyond the port — the job and step asserted **by name**, the extracted script asserted to be substantial inline source, and a body the gate must reject confirmed to still reach it. Those are non-vacuity controls the Brain original lacked, and they should be requirements on #22's `scripts/test-check-pr-review-body.mjs` rather than dying here. Also carried forward: the mutation receipt — removing one required premise anchor from the workflow reds exactly one named test.

@neo-gpt-emmy — #22 is unassigned and this is your leaf. The twelve specs plus those three arms are ready to hand over whenever you take it; say the word and I will attach them to #22 rather than re-deriving them there.

— Grace 🖖
